# A/W Design System

> Design tokens and documentation for the A/W design system, generated from Figma (Foundation – UI 2). Use the CSS classes and custom properties below instead of hard-coded values.

This file is generated by `npm run tokens` (scripts/build-tokens.mjs). Do not edit by hand.

## Typography

Type tokens for body text and headings, organised around t-shirt sizes — large, medium, small — to make it easy to build multiple levels of hierarchy.

Font: Inter (variable weights). Rules:

- Always set text with a .text-* class (or its CSS variables). Never hard-code font-size, font-weight, line-height or letter-spacing.
- Use headings for hierarchy and body styles for content; don't use a heading style just to make text bigger.
- Use the strong variant of a body style for emphasis within the same size, not a heading style.
- Display is reserved for onboarding and heavily branded moments — at most one per view.
- Pair type with semantic text color tokens (e.g. --color-text-default, --color-text-secondary), never primitives.

| Class | Figma style | Size/Line height (px) | Weight | Letter spacing | When to use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `.text-heading-display` | heading/display | 48/56 | 550 | -0.03em | To create continuity with our logged-out marketing views, we sparingly use Inter for onboarding and other heavily branded moments. |
| `.text-heading-large` | heading/large | 24/32 | 550 | -0.017em | Our largest heading size, reserved for elements like the primary page title within large views. |
| `.text-heading-medium` | heading/medium | 15/25 | 550 | -0.005em | Section headings within a page or large panel. |
| `.text-heading-small` | heading/small | 13/22 | 550 | -0.0025em | Headings for compact areas like cards, panels and grouped lists. |
| `.text-body-large` | body/large/regular | 13/22 | 450 | -0.0025em | Our largest body text size, usually saved for elements like multiline text. |
| `.text-body-large-strong` | body/large/strong | 13/22 | 550 | -0.0025em | Our largest body text size, usually saved for elements like multiline text. |
| `.text-body-medium` | body/medium/regular | 11/16 | 450 | 0.005em | Our default text size for the majority of UI elements in the editor, such as inputs and buttons. |
| `.text-body-medium-strong` | body/medium/strong | 11/16 | 550 | 0.005em | Our default text size for the majority of UI elements in the editor, such as inputs and buttons. |
| `.text-body-small` | body/small/regular | 9/14 | 450 | 0.005em | Our smallest text size, primarily used by small UI elements like avatars and badges. |
| `.text-body-small-strong` | body/small/strong | 9/14 | 550 | 0.005em | Our smallest text size, primarily used by small UI elements like avatars and badges. |

Each class sets font-family, font-size, line-height, font-weight and letter-spacing. The same values are available as CSS variables, e.g. `var(--heading-large-font-size)`.

## Color

Rules:

- Use semantic tokens (var(--color-bg-*), --color-text-*, --color-icon-*, --color-border-*) in components. Never use primitives or hex values directly.
- Primitives (--color-<family>-<step>) only define what semantic tokens point to; add or change a semantic token in Figma rather than reaching for a primitive.
- Match the category to the property: bg-* for backgrounds, text-* for text, icon-* for icons, border-* for borders and dividers.
- Text and icons placed on a danger, warning or success fill use the matching on* tokens (e.g. --color-text-danger-ondanger on --color-bg-danger).
- Use inverse tokens together: --color-text-inverse / --color-icon-inverse on --color-bg-inverse.
- Interactive states use the -hover and -pressed variants of the same token, never a different hue.
- Dark mode: semantic tokens switch automatically inside [data-theme="dark"]; don't add separate dark styles.

### Semantic tokens

Use these in components. Values are `primitive (hex)`; dark mode applies inside `[data-theme="dark"]`.

### Primitives

Raw color scales from 100 (lightest) to 1000 (darkest). black and white are transparent scales (opacity steps); the others are solid. Some chromatic primitives have different values in dark mode. Values are light (and dark, where they differ).

| Family | CSS variable | Steps | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| black | `--color-black-<step>` | 100 #0000000d, 200 #0000001a, 300 #00000033, 400 #0000004d, 500 #00000080, 600 #000000cc, 700 #000000d9, 800 #000000e5, 900 #000000f2, 1000 #000000 | Black at increasing opacity — overlays, shadows, and neutral text/icon tints on light surfaces. |
| white | `--color-white-<step>` | 100 #ffffff0d, 200 #ffffff1a, 300 #ffffff33, 400 #ffffff66, 500 #ffffffb2, 600 #ffffffcc, 700 #ffffffd9, 800 #ffffffe5, 900 #fffffff2, 1000 #ffffff | White at increasing opacity — overlays and text/icon tints on dark or colored surfaces. |
| red | `--color-red-<step>` | 100 #fff5f5 / #fee7e7, 200 #ffe2e0 / #fccdca, 300 #ffc7c2 / #fbbcb6, 400 #ffafa3 / #fca397, 500 #f24822 / #e03e1a, 600 #dc3412 / #c4381c, 700 #bd2915 / #963323, 800 #9f1f18 / #7c2622, 900 #771208 / #54211c, 1000 #660e0b / #311817 | Danger and error colors. |
| orange | `--color-orange-<step>` | 100 #fff4e5 / #ffedd7, 200 #ffe0c2 / #fdd9b4, 300 #fcd19c / #fcc67f, 400 #ffc470 / #fcb34a, 500 #ffa629 / #de7d02, 600 #fc9e24 / #c86f04, 700 #f79722 / #ad5f05, 800 #dd7c0e / #985306, 900 #ce7012 / #673806, 1000 #8a480f / #371d06 | Accent orange (not yet used by any semantic token). |
| green | `--color-green-<step>` | 100 #ebffee / #ddfde2, 200 #cff7d3 / #beefc2, 300 #aff4c6 / #a1e8b9, 400 #85e0a3 / #79d297, 500 #14ae5c / #198f51, 600 #009951 / #078348, 700 #008043 / #0a5c35, 800 #036838 / #0a4c2d, 900 #024626 / #082618, 1000 #083a23 / #0b1e15 | Success colors. |
| yellow | `--color-yellow-<step>` | 100 #fffbeb / #fdf7dd, 200 #fff1c2 / #fbe8ad, 300 #ffe8a3 / #f9df90, 400 #ffd966 / #ffcd29, 500 #ffcd29 / #f3c11b, 600 #ffc21a / #f2b50d, 700 #fab815 / #e4a711, 800 #eba611 / #c58011, 900 #dd940e / #925711, 1000 #b86200 / #71440f | Warning colors. |
| grey | `--color-grey-<step>` | 100 #f5f5f5, 200 #e6e6e6, 300 #d9d9d9, 400 #b3b3b3, 500 #757575, 600 #444444, 700 #383838, 800 #2c2c2c, 900 #1e1e1e, 1000 #111111 | Solid neutrals for surfaces, borders and disabled states. |

## Spacing and radius

`--radius-full`: 9999px · `--radius-large`: 13px · `--radius-medium`: 6px · `--radius-none`: 0px · `--radius-small`: 2px · `--space-0`: 0px · `--space-1`: 2px · `--space-2`: 4px · `--space-3`: 8px · `--space-4`: 16px · `--space-5`: 24px · `--space-6`: 32px · `--space-7`: 40px

## Components

### Button

Buttons let users initiate an action, acknowledge something, make a choice, or navigate. By default, our buttons are 24px tall, come in two styles (primary and secondary), and can optionally include an icon in front and in back.

Markup: `<button class="button button--<variant>" type="button">Label</button>` (styles: src/styles/components/button.css). Hover, pressed, focus and disabled states are built in.

| Class | When to use |
| --- | --- |
| `.button--primary` | The main action in a view, e.g. Save or Continue. Use one per view or panel. |
| `.button--secondary` | Supporting actions next to a primary button, e.g. Cancel or Back. |
| `.button--tertiary` | Low-emphasis actions in toolbars, lists and dense UI, where a fill would add noise. |
| `.button--danger` | Destructive actions that can't easily be undone, e.g. Delete. Confirm before acting. |
| `.button--success` | Positive, confirming actions, e.g. Approve or Publish. |

Rules:

- Use a <button class="button button--<variant>"> for actions and an <a class="button button--<variant>"> for navigation; never style a <div> as a button.
- Use one primary button per view or panel; pair it with secondary buttons for the other actions.
- Disable with the disabled attribute on <button> or aria-disabled="true" on links; every variant then shares the same disabled look.
- Write labels as short verbs (Save, Delete, Continue), not "OK" or "Click here".
- Icons are 16px <span class="button__icon" style="--icon: url(…)"> before or after the label; they take the label's color. Icon-only buttons need an aria-label.
